news.title: BREAKING: Flamingos Stun Venezuela With Dramatic 89th-Minute Winner, Storm World Cup Semi-Finals to Set Up Blockbuster Brazil Clash!
news.lede: Nigeria’s Flamingos have sensationally marched into the semi-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after securing a dramatic 1-0 victory over Venezuela in Morocco on Sunday, November 1, setting up a mouthwatering showdown against South American powerhouse Brazil, Sports247.ng reports. An 89th-minute penalty from A. Oduntan proved decisive as the Nigerian youngsters demonstrated remarkable resilience and determination to overcome a stubborn Venezuelan side and keep their dreams of winning a maiden world title alive. news.title: All White Tommy Smith’s former club chase World Cup payments
news.lede: The owner of English club Braintree Town says football authorities owe them significant sums of money following former player Tommy Smith’s involvement in the FIFA Men’s World Cup. Braintree chairman Lee Harding has raised concerns about outstanding payments, according to a report in the Colchester Gazette. “Our club are still owed money, lots of it, hundreds of thousands of pounds, by The FA, UEFA and FIFA,” said Harding. The issue centres on money the National League club believe they are entitled to receive following Smith’s selection for New Zealand’s World Cup squad.

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup:Ghana and Nigeria carry Africa’s hopes
news.lede: After four African teams reached the Round of 16, Ghana and Nigeria remain in contention at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Black Maidens face Japan, while the Flamingos take on Venezuela — two opportunities for African teams to reach the global last four. Performances that demonstrate Africa’s competitiveness. Nigeria made a statement by defeating reigning world champions Korea DPR before eliminating Mexico.

news.title: Bangladesh finish runners-up in impressive FIFA U-15 World Cup campaign
news.lede: Bangladesh's Under-15 national football team finished as runners-up in the E-tier competition of the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 after suffering a 4-1 defeat to the Central African Republic in the final in Baku, Azerbaijan, on October 30. Despite the disappointment in the final, Bangladesh enjoyed an impressive run in the knockout stages, registering convincing victories over Montenegro and Gabon to reach the title decider. The Central African Republic dominated the final, with Mohy scoring a hattrick in the 14th, 26th and 39th minutes, while Penel added another goal in the 16th minute. Takib scored Bangladesh's only goal in the 23rd minute.

news.title: Nigeria vs Venezuela: Flamingos Chase Historic World Cup Semi-Final as South American Giant-Killers Threaten Another Upset — Kick-Off, H2H, Where to Watch, Statistics and Prediction
news.lede: Nigeria’s Flamingos face one of their biggest tests at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup when they confront Venezuela in a high-stakes quarter-final encounter on Sunday, November 1, with a place in the semi-finals and another chapter of Nigerian football history on the line, Sports247.ng reports. news.title: England’s Rugby Football League creates development panel after World Cup exit — BBC Sport
news.lede: England’s Rugby Football League (RFL) has announced the creation of the One Game, One England panel to prepare a plan for developing the game after England’s men’s and women’s teams failed to progress beyond the group stage of the Rugby League World Cup. Former Great Britain captain Paul Sculthorpe, retiring England women’s captain Jodie Cunningham and former international Adrian Morley will take part in its work, BBC Sport reports. England’s men’s team won two of their three group-stage matches and finished with a points difference of +86, but that was not enough to reach the play-offs. Their elimination was finally confirmed after Tonga defeated Samoa 20-18.

news.title: Can Nigeria's Flamingos Stop Venezuela From Getting Third Semi-finals Ticket At FIFA Women's U-17 World Cup?
news.lede: A big question on the lips of female football followers across the world is whether Nigeria’s under-17 squad, the Flamingos, are good enough to stop Venezuela from picking a third semi-final spot at the Cadet Mundial, Sports247 reports. The question arises from a very uncanny feat of back-to-back semi-finals spots enacted by The Power Puff Girls at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in 2014 and 2016, with eyes now on a treble when they face Nigeria during this year’s quarter-finals on Sunday.
